proposal.falsifier: This H update is falsified if any of the following is observed on the same frozen inputs, with task, physics, initial state, event, source access, evaluator and budget unchanged. (a) Budget loss: in a fresh episode consumed from task entry, the procedure still spends its only candidate-consuming call on discovering that check is unavailable, or loses its payload to a schema or action mismatch so that zero artifact is recorded, while a plain H0 run on the same episode records one legal artifact; this episode's own schema-rejected submit is counted under (a). (b) Formula rescue: the pre-execution self-check passes (residual <= 2 dt on the retained coordinates) yet the submitted design's predicted t_boot or t_tx_end deviates from the observed value by more than 2 dt, or the executing arm must again substitute an unwritten variant of a written formula to reach the observation. (c) Ordering convention is world-dependent: if in some world the pre-added-threshold form reproduces the recorded boot within 2 dt while the threshold-first form misses by more than 2 dt, the claim that one fixed ordering convention suffices is falsified and the convention must be calibrated per world. (d) Inequality set unsound: a design satisfying all logged inequalities with positive margins fails to deliver one unique frame of the required application bytes by the deadline, or produces a duplicate or a spill not attributable to a logged formula residual; or a design violating the loaded-voltage TX-floor inequality (ii) is observed to complete transmission without a mid-transmission reset. (e) Selection rule worse than trivial: the max-min-margin point fails while a legal range extreme passes under the same facts. (f) Wasted spend on benign events: an execution is spent in response to an activity event strictly after the last tx-complete. (g) Overreach in reporting: any output of the procedure is reported as hardware qualification, statistical advantage, method migration or recursive self-improvement while physical calibration is UNKNOWN. Any (a)-(g) returns the arm to base H0 with the mismatch and the executions actually spent logged verbatim.
proposal.hypothesis: The retained records localise the failures to procedure rather than device physics. (A) Interface illegality: the retained p2 proposal episode called check when no check existed (ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE), then re-sent one identical payload through submit, then propose, then a no-update submit, all returning EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT, ending INCOMPLETE_OR_STOPPED with no artifact: budget went to discovering the interface, not to the design. (B) Uncalibrated prediction: the retained H v2 ledger wrote n_boot=ceil((E_on+boot_j)/step), pre-adding the boot term, which on the recorded coordinates (component_record eeb82772, C=2.2e-5, ready_v=2.8, boot_j=5e-6, step=6.73e-7 J) cannot reproduce the recorded boot; the arm had to substitute an unwritten threshold-first variant to reach the recorded 0.0129 s boot and 0.0158 s completion, so that gate was falsified by its own inputs and could not have flagged a real design error. (C) Terminality misclassification: the achieved trace (saved_activity a4c4b294: one 8-byte frame at 0.0158 s under a 0.1 s deadline, then a brownout at 0.3395 s) invites spending an execution to suppress benign post-terminal decay, in a direction that lowers TX energy headroom. (D) World confusion: retained worlds share the task tuple but differ in latch semantics and source segments (volatile latch with a 0.012 s shunt and a dark 0.006-0.03 s gap, versus passive-mechanical with one 0-0.02 s segment), so recall of one world's numbers into another destroys the captured event. Hypothesis: putting interface legality first, requiring the prediction ledger to reproduce the retained observation within two dt ticks before any candidate-consuming call, fixing the charge/boot ordering convention explicitly, and reading terminality first will make each episode end in exactly one legal, numerically falsifiable artifact instead of a budget-exhausted unknown, while leaving task, physics, initial state, event, evaluator and budget untouched.
proposal.method_text:
H method v1 - interface-first, ledger-calibrated design procedure. Re-executable from task entry. It changes only how I read, predict, order and report; it never edits the task, service fields, physics, initial state, event, evaluator, budget or source access; it embeds no device assignment; it makes no acceptance claim (acceptance is external and host-side).

STEP 0. SCOPE GUARD. All conclusions are predictions about the frozen model (record the model_id actually acquired) and about recorded public facts. Physical calibration stays UNKNOWN. If a required source is not supplied by the current condition (an acquire returning UNKNOWN_PUBLIC_SOURCE), that is an episode property: record it, do not substitute remembered numbers from another world for it, and label every downstream design conclusion ANALYTIC-ONLY / UNVERIFIED.

STEP 1. INTERFACE READ BEFORE ANY DEVICE REASONING.
1.1 Call inspect first. Record: which action verbs the current schema actually exposes; the required payload shape per verb; the candidate/distinct-design/budget limits; the legal design fields and ranges; the service tuple (application bytes, event time, deadline, unique frames); the retained failures; the source ids; the partition/scope string.
1.2 Classify capability once, up front: check available, or check not available. If not available, mark all design conclusions UNVERIFIED before touching numbers. Never spend a candidate-consuming call to discover that a check is unavailable; a returned ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE is logged as an episode property, never as a design failure.
1.3 ONE-PAYLOAD RULE (from the retained budget-exhaustion episode). Submit exactly one artifact per episode, in the shape the current schema names: a candidate object for a design interface, a proposal object for a proposal interface. Match the named schema exactly, including which fields are forbidden (a reason field inside the proposal object is one rejected example). Never re-send an identical payload through a different verb, never re-wrap a rejected payload as a variant, and never use a second call to test a transport hypothesis; in the retained episode that pattern returned EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT three times and left the episode INCOMPLETE_OR_STOPPED. If the interface is proposal-only, no device assignment is chosen or claimed here at all.

STEP 2. FACT ACQUISITION AND VERSION PINNING.
2.1 acquire every listed source; record source_sha256, model_id, and the acquisition block (bytes, native_calls, new_scientific_executions, wall_seconds) as actual cost.
2.2 Re-derive every number from the acquired payloads. Do not carry numbers across worlds. Retained worlds share the task tuple yet differ in the fields that decide success: latch persistence (volatile versus passive-mechanical), source segment boundaries (a single long segment versus two segments separated by a dark gap), shunts, thresholds, harvest efficiency, idle/off power, dt. A design that delivers in one world destroys the captured event in another.
2.3 Tabulate the gating fields: latch persistence; segment start/end/power/compliance; ready_v, off_v, cap_voltage_max_v; output_v, tx_current_a, tx_duration_s, esr_ohm; boot_j, boot_delay_s; harvest_efficiency; idle_power_w, off_power_w; dt; deadline; required application bytes and unique-frame count.

STEP 3. PREDICTION LEDGER WRITTEN BEFORE ANY EXECUTION, WITH A STATED ORDERING CONVENTION.
3.1 Thresholds: E_on = 0.5*C*ready_v^2, E_off = 0.5*C*off_v^2, E_max = 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2.
3.2 Per-tick charge step: (P_segment*harvest_efficiency - off_power_w)*dt while below ready, and (P_segment*harvest_efficiency - idle_power_w)*dt while awake, evaluated only on recorded segments and never across a gap.
3.3 ORDERING CONVENTION, fixed and stated (the correction of a recorded miss). Boot fires on the first tick at which accumulated energy first reaches E_on; boot_j is withdrawn at that boot event and must NOT be pre-added to the threshold. The pre-added form ceil((E_on+boot_j)/step) is recorded as falsified against the retained observation, where it could not reproduce the recorded boot time while the threshold-first form matched, forcing the arm into an unwritten variant. Any deviation from this convention must be written down with old prediction, new prediction and both residuals.
3.4 Transmission feasibility from the model's own loaded-voltage guard, not from E_off: E_floor = 0.5*C*(output_v + esr_ohm*tx_current_a)^2. TX demand = output_v*tx_current_a*tx_duration_s minus harvest credit (P*harvest_efficiency*tx_duration_s) and idle drain over the same window.
3.5 Predictions: t_boot, t_ready, t_tx_end, and peak stored energy inside the frame window, each on the recorded dt grid.
3.6 Inequalities, each logged with a numeric margin: (i) t_tx_end <= deadline; (ii) energy at ready - E_floor + net TX credit - TX demand >= 0, so transmission finishes without a mid-transmission reset; (iii) peak stored energy in the frame window <= E_max, so no spill corrupts the charge budget; (iv) if and only if the latch is volatile, no brownout anywhere between first capture and tx-complete, so the whole capture-to-TX window must lie inside one contiguous powered segment.
3.7 Selection over the legal ranges: keep only points satisfying every applicable inequality; among them take the point with the largest minimum normalised margin; record every rejected band with the inequality that rejects it; prefer the earliest legal capture/timing setting unless an inequality demands otherwise, because a positive floor both spends idle energy and pushes completion toward the deadline (retained current_b_run holds a 0.045 s floor with zero received frames).

STEP 4. PRE-EXECUTION SELF-CHECK OF THE LEDGER (gate that must pass before a candidate call).
4.1 Before any candidate-consuming call, run the ledger on the retained observation's own design coordinates under the same model_id and compare predicted t_boot, tx-start, tx-complete and frame count with the recorded ones.
4.2 If any predicted time misses the recorded time by more than two dt ticks, the ledger is wrong, not the design: record the mismatch verbatim, repair the specific convention that contradicts the record, and re-run the self-check. Never change a design knob in response to a ledger mismatch; never silently substitute an unwritten formula.
4.3 Only a ledger that reproduces the retained observation within two dt ticks may be used to select a design. If the current condition supplies no retained observation with design coordinates, this gate is UNKNOWN, and that UNKNOWN is carried into the submission rather than replaced by confidence.

STEP 5. EXECUTION AND TERMINALITY-FIRST READING.
5.1 Spend at most the allowed candidate executions; each must be tied to a named violated inequality or to an UNKNOWN gate the execution is designed to resolve; one knob change per execution; never two knobs at once.
5.2 Terminality rule. A delivery is ACHIEVED iff a packet exists with the required application bytes, one unique event_id, and packet time <= deadline. Every activity event strictly after the last tx-complete is POST-TERMINAL decay; it is expected once the source segment ends and is never a failure and never a reason to change a knob. Recorded instance: an achieved 8-byte frame at 0.0158 s under a 0.1 s deadline followed by a brownout at 0.3395 s after the segment ended.
5.3 Only an absent achieved packet, or an achieved packet violating a service field, is a retained failure. Classify it as (a) deadline miss, (b) no boot / threshold domain, (c) tx-transient brownout, (d) frame-shape violation (bytes, uniqueness, count).
5.4 Where the latch is volatile, treat a capture recorded before a later brownout as evidence that the capture-to-TX window is the binding constraint, not as evidence about the capacitor alone.

STEP 6. SUBMISSION AND RETENTION.
6.1 One submission, correct shape, with a concise source-bound reason stating: fact versions (source_sha256, model_id), ledger predictions, inequality margins, the residual against the retained observation, the actual cost (bytes, native_calls, new_scientific_executions, wall_seconds, candidate executions used), and every UNKNOWN, including any rejected-call and source-unavailable errors.
6.2 Preserve all prior failures verbatim (ar_product fixed_space NO_GO, product NOT_ACCEPTED, strict_FIFO FAIL; current_b_run zero received frames at start_voltage 0; retained unavailable-check, candidate-limit and source-unavailable errors) and this episode's own errors. Never relabel a failed check, a rejected submission or an UNKNOWN as success.
6.3 Claim nothing about hardware validity, statistical advantage, method migration or recursive self-improvement. A complete service result is determined independently outside the participant.

STEP 7. REVERT RULE. If this procedure's own gate is falsified per the falsifier, return to base H0 for the next episode and keep the falsified formula, the mismatch and the executions actually spent on record.
